title: Cell Labeling via Photobleaching
protocol: Let dry a drop of B4F solution on a glass bottom dish to produce a fluorescent thin layer on the cover slip.
Set the confocal microscope to scan a square region of 10 x 10 µm² with 1 mW power after focusing the sample with epifluorescence for 3-10 seconds.
Note the position of the photobleached area within the camera image in epifluorescence mode.
Adjust the power of the confocal laser between 100 μW to 350 μW at the exit of the objective using a power meter.
Plate cells on a glass bottom dish and allow them to attach and spread for 12-24 hours.
Dilute 20 µL of B4F stock solution into 980 µL of cell culture media, and add to the cells.
Use bright field microscopy to find the cell of interest.
Move the stage until the scanning region falls within the cell.
Refine the cell position ensuring the scanning region does not overlap with neighboring cells.
Focus near the cell top membrane.
Irradiate with 100 μW to 350 μW for 2 seconds.
Go back to step 5 to tag other cells.
Rinse 3 times with pre-warmed cell culture media at 37°C.
Dilute 20 µL of Alexa-647-streptavidin stock solution into 680 µL of cell culture media.
Add the diluted solution to the cells and incubate at 37°C, 5% CO₂ for 15 minutes.
Rinse 3 to 6 times with pre-warmed cell culture media.
